overallNotes.personaArc: Derek Anthony Kubik's arc spans 3.5 years (Jan 2025 to May 2028) and follows a coherent journey from frontline journeyman wireman with a concern about training quality to the recognized point person for a permanent, field-trusted first-year apprenticeship pipeline at IBEW Local 5 and the Western Pennsylvania Electrical JATC. The arc has distinct phases: (1) Profile building and relationship mapping (Jan 2025); (2) Incident-triggered reform (near-miss ladder incident, Q1 2025); (3) Pilot design and political navigation (Q2-Q3 2025, with Ron Belski as primary antagonist); (4) First validation and expansion (Q2 2025-Q1 2026); (5) Institutional boundary testing (Q2 2026 summer bridge rejection); (6) System proven and standardized (Q4 2026-Q1 2027); (7) Field credibility and external demand (Q4 2027); (8) Institutionalization (Q1-Q2 2028). Parallel personal arcs include: family financial boundaries with Logan and Marlene (ongoing strain that resolves into structured help), house renovation from perpetual jobsite to functional home, back injury management from denial to consistent care routine, leisure shift from default consumption to intentional hobbies (podcasts, memorabilia collecting, one-sitting films, regional essays), and marriage boundaries solidifying around protected family time.
dataQualityIssues: ALL focus fields are truncated — they begin with 'A lot has shifted lately' or similar openings but cut off mid-sentence before describing the actual topic
ALL summary fields are single-sentence quote fragments from turn 3 of the conversation, not actual summaries of the slice content
ALL emotional_tone values are 'neutral' regardless of the conversation's actual emotional valence — many are clearly positive or mixed
ALL tags are generic single-word categories (work, family, health, finance, etc.) that fail to capture the specific events, decisions, or themes of each slice
Several decision entries are truncated mid-sentence, cutting off the actual decision description
Baseline tag 'leisure' is inconsistently applied — appears on some clearly work-focused slices while missing from genuinely leisure-oriented ones
Multiple slices have completely irrelevant baseline tags (e.g., 'travel' on a back injury conversation)
Slice 2025-01-28 has a decision truncated at 'Der' — barely started
patternNotes: Derek consistently opens conversations with 'A lot has shifted lately' or 'Things have been busy' — this is a personal conversational tic that generates the truncated focus fields
The baseline tag generation algorithm seems to assign all possible categories from a fixed list rather than identifying slice-specific themes
Emotional tone was never meaningfully assessed — all 'neutral' suggests a bug or missing implementation in the tagger
The persona's voice is remarkably consistent: plainspoken, self-aware, practical, with a dry under-pressure humor and a tendency to frame problems as systems to be solved

Key recurring characters: Erin (wife, pragmatic anchor), Logan (brother, recurring financial strain), Mike Cercone (friend, steamfitter, emotional outlet), Ron Belski (veteran instructor, institutional resistance), Tasha Freeman (safety director, field-level ally), Marlene (mother, guilt vector around Logan)

The renovation timeline is a through-line: first-floor hired help completes 2026-04, basement/fence 2028-02, enabling the dog plan — the house literally becomes more livable in parallel with Derek's professional system maturing
overallNotes.strandsComparison: The current strands.json uses the same generic categories as the slice tags (work, family, health, finance, etc.). A more useful strand system would use specific thematic threads: apprenticeship-reform-arc, back-injury-management, family-financial-boundaries, house-renovation-progress, collecting-hobby-emergence, marriage-relationship-maintenance, entertainment-preference-shift, reading-preference-shift. These eight threads would more accurately represent the actual narrative content.
